summary: Background metrics emitter from customer sidecar causing uneven GPU banking and autoscaler under-provisioning
description:
Issue summary: High p99 latency and intermittent 429s observed on Flowly AI's dedicated pool starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC. Symptoms correspond with gradual GPU allocation failures and autoscaler failing to add capacity fast enough.

Observed impact: Customer reports increased request timeouts and error spikes for their production chat endpoint. Multiple model routes degraded concurrently in us-west-2.

Initial detection: Alerting (p99 latency > 900ms and allocation-failures > 5/min) triggered on our production observability pipeline at 2026-03-10 09:18 UTC.
impact: Flowly AI (dedicated) experienced ~30% increase in p95/p99 latency and transient 429s across two model routes. Throughput dropped by ~25% during hot windows. Business impact: customer-reported degraded UX and elevated error rates for paying customers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Route traffic to the affected dedicated pool in us-west-2. 2) Start synthetic steady small-stream workload that keeps many long-lived keepalives open (simulates chatlet fusion). 3) Run background sidecar process on a tenant VM that emits high-frequency metrics to our sidecar endpoint (~10k metrics/min). 4) Observe allocator logs and autoscaler decisions over 10-20 minutes. Expected: autoscaler should add capacity and allocations succeed; Observed: allocator marks GPUs as temporarily busy and autoscaler remains conservative.
logs:
[2026-03-10T09:16:12Z] allocator: attach_request(id=abc123) -> timeout after 1.5s
[2026-03-10T09:16:13Z] serving-runtime: nvlink_io_wait=0.28s, dma_queue=high, gpu_attach_retries=3
[2026-03-10T09:17:02Z] autoscaler: candidate_addition=0 (policy: conservative), pending_queue=14
[2026-03-10T09:17:05Z] allocator: observed_bank_busy(gpu=GPU-75, bank=2) repeated=7
[2026-03-10T09:18:03Z] sidecar-metrics: recv_metrics(rate=10200/min) from tenant=flowly-sidecar-3
[2026-03-10T09:18:10Z] error: 429 route=flowly-chat model=gpt-3o-redwood-v1
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: a tenant sidecar emitting a very high cardinality metrics stream is saturating the allocator's NVLink / PCIe servicing path and causing per-GPU bank busy signals. This produces intermittent attach failures which the autoscaler interprets as transient and does not scale quickly.

What we checked: allocator attach/fail counters, NVLink PCIe backlog metrics, kernel logs on affected hosts, autoscaler decision logs, and Flowly's sidecar process (customer-provided) traffic. Cross-referenced with host-level iostat and nvidia-smi dmon.

Findings:
- The allocator showed repeated bank_busy signals localized to a subset of GPUs on three nodes.
- Network/IO saturation coincides with sidecar metric bursts (approx 10k/min) from Flowly's VM.
- Autoscaler has a smoothing window (cooldown 90s) and a conservative threshold for attachments failing (requires sustained failure rate) which delayed capacity additions.
- No driver crashes or CUDA OOM; NVLink latency elevated and DMA queues backed up during burst windows.
actions_taken:
- Throttled Flowly sidecar metric ingestion by applying per-tenant ingress rate limit at the sidecar proxy (temporary).
- Manually triggered autoscaler to add two GPU slots to the dedicated pool in us-west-2 (immediate relief).
- Marked three affected nodes for deeper hardware IO analysis and temporarily drained low-priority pods.
- Engaged infra team to evaluate allocator NVLink handling and to add finer-grained bank_busy telemetry.
workaround: Applied per-tenant metrics ingestion caps (rate-limited sidecar requests). Customer reverted their sidecar config to emit aggregated metrics (1k/min) which reduced NVLink backlog and restored normal attach rates. Manual scale-up restored throughput while long-term fix is planned.
final_resolution:
PENDING - engineering is implementing two fixes: 1) allocator change to de-prioritize sidecar metric IO on GPU hosts during attach windows; 2) autoscaler tuning to consider attach failure patterns and allow fast-path scale-up for noisy-tenant signatures. Patch PR opened and under review (runtime PR #4512). After patch merge and controlled rollout, we will remove temporary ingress caps and validate for 48 hours.

Follow-ups: runbook update to include noisy-sidecar detection, and discuss quota enforcement for metric streams from tenants.
